title: Divine Protection and Salvation
english: Moreover, about every holy one he sings and says the blessed David, that the Lord's angel encamps around those who fear Him and rescues them.
He will rescue those who hope in Him, and He will cry out to me, and I will answer him.
I am with him in tribulation, and He will glorify them, filling their days with length and showing them His salvation.
But what is this salvation that God and Father offer? It is the Word of God, who became flesh for us.
Through the prophet Isaiah, the Father calls the Son 'salvation,' saying that nations will see His righteousness and kings His glory (Isaiah 60:5).
The Son's salvation will shine like a lamp, illuminating the darkness.
We are justified in Him and have been given the glory of adoption.
We have escaped the bonds of death and risen to incorruption.
The Son has appeared to us as a lamp in the night, giving divine light to believers' souls.
He declares, 'I am the light of the world'.
The persecuted are blessed because they will inherit the heavenly kingdom and have God and Savior as their defender.
They will see the mystery of Christ and learn from Jacob's example.
It is fitting to present the events surrounding Jacob's life in order to provide a more accurate understanding for those who will encounter them.
The story unfolds with Esau's anger towards Jacob, stemming from the blessing their father had given him.
Esau's thoughts were consumed by a desire for revenge, and he awaited the opportunity to strike when his father's mourning period would come to an end.
Rebekah, upon learning of Esau's intentions, quickly summoned her younger son, Jacob, and warned him of the danger that awaited him.
She urged him to flee to Mesopotamia, to the home of her brother, Laban, in the city of Haran.
There, Jacob would remain until Esau's anger had subsided, and the memory of his past actions had faded.
Rebekah reassured Jacob that she would send for him when the time was right, lest she be bereaved of both of you in one day.
Meanwhile, Rebekah approached her husband, Isaac, and said: 'I am grieved with my life because of the daughters of the sons of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of this land…'
The text ends mid-sentence: 'If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of this land…'

title: Moses in Midian and the People of Faith
english: Moses arrived in the land of the Midianites.
He encountered shepherds and the daughters of Jethro, who were being mistreated by the shepherds.
He was recognized for his zeal in rescuing them and watering their flocks, uncovering the depth of the history.
The thoughts and meanings are somehow related and connected, and the things from them are somehow very much related.
Moses had departed from Pharaoh and had settled in the land of Midian.
He came to the land of Midian and sat down by the well.
The priest of Midian had seven daughters, who were shepherding their father's flock.
They came to draw water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
The shepherds came and drove them away.
Moses arose and rescued them, and he watered their flock.
They came to Jethro their father.
He said to them, 'How is it that you have come back so soon today?'
They said, 'An Egyptian man delivered us from the hand of the shepherds, and he drew water for us and watered the flock.'
He said to his daughters, 'Then where is he? Why is it that you have left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.'
Moses dwelt with the man.
Thus you understand how thoughts are akin in a certain way, and how the things signified by them are closely related.
But the divine Moses, having removed the envy of the other shepherds, drew water and gave drink to the flocks of Jethro.
And Jacob alone rolled away the stone, though many were wont not to do this without sweat, and he gave drink likewise to the flocks of Laban.
And just as Moses went down to the well of the idolatrous man, so also did the divine Jacob.
For Laban was still a worshipper of idols and a servant of them.
But since the word has put on the face and shape of the people of faith toward Jacob, let us say the inner and hidden things, uncovering the depth of the history.

The people being formed, according to the voice of the Psalmist, would be no other, I think, than the new one in Christ, that is, the one who has been brought into the glory of the firstborn through faith, with the first having been pushed aside and Israel having slipped.
For the one who was the head, that is, the one who was prominent, and the one who was foreknown, is said to be the follower of the calling of the others.
They are placed on the back, and they heal after the nations.
Therefore, the people in Christ through faith are a heel, and they have been reckoned as in order according to the divine Jacob.
Let us think of the chorus of the holy apostles as the firstfruits of this kind, who were from the blood and nation of Israel.
Since they have been enriched with faith in Christ, and have put on the grace of the Holy Spirit like a crown, they have been added to those from the nation.
They leave behind those who are murderers and have been completely softened, becoming gentle…
translator_notes: The source text begins with a fragment: 'ἰς τὴν τῶν Μαδιηναίων ἀφικνεῖται χώραν.' which appears to be missing an initial vowel, likely intending 'Ἐις'. Rendered literally with leading ellipsis as per edge fragment handling.
The source text ends mid-sentence with 'καταλιμπάνουσι, μονονουχ' which is incomplete; rendered with trailing ellipsis as per edge fragment handling.

title: Bridegroom and Church
english: The bridegroom, who comes from above and from heaven, is united with the Church from the nations. This union is forever, and it is characterized by righteousness, judgment, mercy, and compassions. The Church is betrothed to the Lord in faith, and through this faith, she comes to know him. However, the older Church, which was led before the Church from the nations, did not remain in this union forever. The Lord said of her, 'She is not my wife,' and 'I am not her husband.' He also gave her a certificate of divorce, for she had been cast out like an adulteress and condemned for her loud cries.

The Lord rebukes the older Church, saying, 'You have committed adultery with many shepherds, and you return to me.' He calls her to lift up her eyes and see where she has been corrupted. She has defiled the land with her adulteries and evils, and she has had many shepherds as a stumbling block for herself. Her appearance has become like that of a shameless prostitute. The Lord asks, 'Will this not remain forever?' But in contrast to the older Church, the younger Church, which is the Church from the nations, betroths herself to the Lord continually.

God betrothed the synagogue of the Jews through Moses as a mediator, but He was also united with the church from the Gentiles, calling her with His own voice and being seen by one of the men on earth. He bowed down to the bride who was crying out, and He was heard by those who spoke in the past, but only through Moses or the prophets.

In the last times, the Son spoke to us directly, as Paul the wise also testified. It is also fitting to consider the origin of the sons of Jacob, how many and from whom they came. Leah first gave birth to four sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah. Since Rachel was barren and childless, she devised a plan to have children, persuading Jacob to go to her servant Bilhah, who gave birth to two sons, Dan and Naphtali, upon my loins. Leah also gave birth to Ziphrah, her own...
translator_notes: The Greek text is fragmented at the beginning and end.
The translation of 'ἐξ ἐθνῶν' as 'from the Gentiles' is an idiomatic expression for non-Jews.
The phrase 'μεσίτου Μωσέως' is translated as 'through Moses as a mediator' to reflect Moses' role as a mediator between the Jewish people and God.
The metaphor of the 'νύμφῃ βοώσῃ' is translated as 'to the bride who was crying out' to convey the idea of the church or the people of God crying out to God.
The final fragment 'Λεία γε μὴν Ζελφὰν τὴν ἑαυ' is rendered as 'Leah also gave birth to Ziphrah, her own...' to reflect the incomplete text.
